zones.what: Lifeboats are mounted at Deck 5; they obstruct the downward view from Decks 6, 7, and 8, with Deck 6 most affected and obstruction decreasing as you go higher.
zones.effect: You'll see the horizon and ocean clearly, but looking straight down you'll see orange lifeboat roofs instead of water—Deck 6 cabins look almost directly at the boat tops.
zones.mattersTo: Matters to photographers and anyone who wants an unobstructed view straight down to the waterline; doesn't matter if you care more about horizon views and sunsets.

zones.what: Resort Deck (Deck 14) sits directly above Deck 12 mid and aft sections, with the main pool, Rooftop Garden, and pool bar creating daytime foot traffic and activity.
zones.effect: You may hear poolside music, deck furniture being moved, and crowd noise during the day, typically quieting after evening; the activity is directly overhead.
zones.mattersTo: Light sleepers and anyone planning to nap or relax in their cabin during the day should avoid these; evening-only cabin users won't notice.

zones.what: The spa, thermal suite, and adjacent Solarium are located on Deck 12 directly above portions of Deck 11 mid and aft.
zones.effect: Potential for spa treatment room activity, foot traffic, and water feature sounds from the Solarium during spa operating hours directly overhead.
zones.mattersTo: Light sleepers who are in their cabin during daytime hours; most guests out exploring won't be affected.

zones.what: The main theater (theater deck and balcony seating) is located on Decks 4 and 5, two to three decks below the forward cabins on Decks 7 and 8.
zones.effect: Show audio and bass can sometimes transmit upward during evening performances, though the distance (2-3 decks) significantly dampens the effect.
zones.mattersTo: Sensitive sleepers who turn in before 10 PM might notice; most guests attending shows or late dining won't be in their cabins during performance times.

zones.what: The main dining room spans Decks 3 and 4, multiple decks below mid and aft cabin sections on Decks 8, 9, and 10.
zones.effect: The multi-deck distance makes noise transmission unlikely, but very sensitive guests might detect faint kitchen or service activity during early morning breakfast prep or late dinner service.
zones.mattersTo: Only the most noise-sensitive guests; the distance makes this a non-issue for the vast majority.

zones.what: Primary elevator banks run through the midship section on all guest cabin decks, with the main bank centrally located near the Grand Plaza.
zones.effect: Cabins very close to elevator lobbies offer unbeatable convenience but may hear door chimes, mechanical sounds, and hallway conversation at all hours; cabins further along corridors are quieter but require more walking.
zones.mattersTo: Mobility-challenged guests and those prioritizing convenience should seek elevator-adjacent cabins; light sleepers should avoid the immediate elevator lobby area.

zones.what: Deck 3 aft cabins (8 cabins total) sit relatively low and toward the stern, closer to propulsion machinery spaces.
zones.effect: These cabins may experience more low-frequency vibration and mechanical hum than higher or more forward locations, particularly noticeable at cruising speed.
zones.mattersTo: Vibration-sensitive guests should avoid; those who aren't bothered by white noise or who want the lowest-priced ocean views may find this a fair trade.

zones.what: Deck 3 forward cabins sit low at the bow where bow thruster operation during docking and maneuvering creates mechanical noise and vibration.
zones.effect: You'll hear and feel the thrusters during port arrivals and departures—typically early morning and evening—with a grinding or rumbling sensation that can be startling if you're unaware.
zones.mattersTo: Light sleepers and early risers in port-heavy itineraries should avoid; doesn't matter at sea or for guests who sleep through mechanical sounds.

zones.what: Forward sections on these decks are near the anchor chain machinery, which operates during every port arrival as the anchor is deployed.
zones.effect: Early morning arrivals in port bring loud chain-running noise—a distinctive grinding and rattling that can wake even sound sleepers, typically between 6-7 AM.
zones.mattersTo: Anyone who values sleeping in on port days should avoid forward cabins on these decks; early risers and port-focused cruisers won't mind.

zones.what: Deck 9 midship sits directly below the Grand Plaza atrium on Deck 10, a social hub with bars and often live music.
zones.effect: Music, conversation, and foot traffic from the Grand Plaza can transmit downward during evening hours when the atrium is most active, typically until 11 PM or midnight.
zones.mattersTo: Early sleepers should avoid; guests who are out enjoying evening entertainment won't be in their cabins during the noisy hours.

zones.what: The Edge Villas on Deck 15 sit directly above the Rooftop Garden and Resort Deck pool area, with two decks of separation.
zones.effect: Pool music, activity, and crowd noise may be faintly audible on the villa terraces during peak daytime hours, though the two-deck separation significantly dampens the effect.
zones.mattersTo: Villa guests seeking absolute tranquility on their terrace during peak pool hours might notice; most won't find it intrusive given the separation and villa insulation.
